title: Pagination
description: Implement paginated queries with keepPreviousData for smooth page transitions.

data.text: Pagination with React Query means including the page number in the query key so that each page is cached separately. The `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` option ensures the old page data remains visible while the new page loads â€” eliminating the jarring flash of a loading state.
How Pagination Works with React Query

When the user clicks "Next", the page state updates. React Query detects that the queryKey has changed (e.g., from ['users', 1] to ['users', 2]) and fetches the new page. Because the old page data is still in the cache, placeholderData: keepPreviousData returns it immediately while the new request is in flight.

data.caption: Data flow when the user navigates between paginated pages
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Component
    participant RQ as React Query Cache
    participant S as Server
    U->>C: Click "Next" â†’ page = 2
    C->>RQ: useQuery(['users', 2]) â€” cache miss
    RQ->>S: GET /api/users?page=2
    Note over C,RQ: keepPreviousData shows page 1
    C->>U: Render page 1 data (placeholder)
    S-->>RQ: Return page 2 data
    RQ->>RQ: Cache page 2
    RQ->>C: Deliver page 2 data
    C->>U: Render page 2 data

data.text: The paginated query function receives a page parameter. Use useState to track the current page, include it in the queryKey, and use keepPreviousData to preserve the previous page's UI during the fetch.

data.title: Paginated Users List
isPlaceholderData Flag
data.text: When keepPreviousData is active, isPlaceholderData is true. Use it to show a loading indicator, disable navigation buttons, or apply a subtle opacity change to indicate the data is not yet confirmed.

Keep the page number in useState. When the user navigates to a new page, the state updates, the queryKey changes, and React Query creates a new cache entry. Previous pages remain cached and can be revisited instantly.

data.title: Pagination Best Practices
items: Use a separate queryKey per page: ['items', 'list', page]
Use keepPreviousData to prevent the loading flash between pages
Disable the Next button while isPlaceholderData is true to prevent double-fetches
Show a page indicator so users know where they are in the result set
Disable Previous on page 1 and Next on the last page

terms.definition: A special placeholderData value in React Query v5 that returns the previous query result while a new page loads. Eliminates the loading flash during pagination.
A boolean flag set to true when the displayed data came from placeholderData (not the real cache). Use it to show subtle loading indicators during pagination transitions.
Including the page number in the queryKey array (e.g., ['items', page]) so React Query caches each page independently.

data.text: Most paginated APIs accept page and limit parameters. Pass these as part of the queryKey so that changing the page size also triggers a refetch. React Query cancels the in-flight request automatically when the key changes.

data.title: Build a Paginated Article List
data.description: Create a paginated article list that fetches from a mock API. Implement smooth page transitions with keepPreviousData and a page size selector.
steps: Create a mock API fetchArticles(page, limit) that returns articles, totalCount, and totalPages after a 400ms delay
Create a PaginatedArticles component with useState for page and limit
Use useQuery with queryKey ['articles', 'list', page, limit]
Apply placeholderData: keepPreviousData for smooth transitions
Show 'Loading next page...' when isPlaceholderData is true
Add Previous/Next buttons with correct disabled states
Add a page size selector (5, 10, 20) that resets to page 1 on change
Style the pagination bar with Tailwind CSS
data.expectedOutcome: A paginated article list with no loading flash between pages, a working page size selector, and correct button states. Navigating back to page 1 after visiting page 3 loads instantly from cache.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Include the page number in the queryKey so each page is cached independently
Use placeholderData: keepPreviousData to show old data during page transitions
isPlaceholderData tells you when placeholder data is being displayed
Keep page state in useState and update it to trigger new fetches
Reset to page 1 when the page size (limit) changes
Each cached page can be revisited instantly without a network request
data.takeaway: Pagination with React Query is simple: include the page in the key, use keepPreviousData, and let the cache handle the rest.
